children.title: Loss Conventions
children.top_down_role: Sign orientation, ordering, and reporting practices when uncertain outcomes are recorded as losses.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign and order convention for random losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal L\) be a linear space of real-valued random losses containing the constants. Larger values represent worse outcomes. A loss-based risk functional is a map \(\rho_L:\mathcal L\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) interpreted so that \(\rho_L(L)\) is the assessed risk of loss \(L\); hence its order convention is \(L_1\le L_2\Rightarrow \rho_L(L_1)\le\rho_L(L_2)\). Under monetary cash translation, adding a sure loss \(m\in\mathbb R\) gives \(\rho_L(L+m)=\rho_L(L)+m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Losses are ordered upward: a larger loss is riskier, and adding a certain loss increases monetary risk by the same amount.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal L\) is a linear space of random variables containing all constants.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The loss-sign convention is mathematically coherent and fits the definition container, but no inspectable source supports the convention or cash-translation formula.

children.title: Reward Conventions
children.top_down_role: Sign orientation, ordering, and reporting practices when uncertain outcomes are recorded as rewards.

knowledge_statements.title: Reward Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign and order convention for random rewards or payoffs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) be a linear space of real-valued random rewards containing the constants. Larger values represent better outcomes. A reward-based risk functional is a map \(\rho_R:\mathcal X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) interpreted so that \(\rho_R(X)\) is the risk of reward \(X\); consequently \(X_1\le X_2\Rightarrow\rho_R(X_1)\ge\rho_R(X_2)\). Under monetary cash translation, adding a sure reward \(m\in\mathbb R\) gives \(\rho_R(X+m)=\rho_R(X)-m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rewards are ordered upward as desirable: a larger payoff is less risky, and added cash reduces monetary risk by the same amount.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is a linear space of random variables containing all constants.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reward convention is precise and correctly reverses monotonicity and cash translation, but it has no cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Loss–Reward Translation
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between loss-based and reward-based risk formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss–Reward Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-change equivalence between loss- and reward-based formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\mathcal X\) is closed under negation and identify the loss associated with reward \(X\) as \(L=-X\). For any loss-convention functional \(\rho_L\), define \(\rho_R(X)=\rho_L(-X)\). Conversely, \(\rho_L(L)=\rho_R(-L)\). This involutive translation converts loss monotonicity into reward antitonicity and converts \(\rho_L(L+m)=\rho_L(L)+m\) into \(\rho_R(X+m)=\rho_R(X)-m\), while preserving convexity and positive homogeneity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing a reward by its negative loss translates the two conventions and preserves the usual convexity and homogeneity axioms.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is a linear space closed under \(X\mapsto-X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sign-change representation is mathematically consistent and fits the translation container, but the asserted preservation of axioms lacks source support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Four axioms for a coherent risk functional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to random variables in the domain of a real-valued risk functional, using first-order stochastic dominance for monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A risk functional R satisfies the four axioms if, for all random variables \xi,\zeta in its domain, all \lambda\ge 0, and all t\in\mathbb{R}: (i) R(\xi+\zeta)\le R(\xi)+R(\zeta); (ii) R(\lambda\xi)=\lambda R(\xi); (iii) \xi\preccurlyeq\zeta\Rightarrow R(\xi)\le R(\zeta), where \xi\preccurlyeq\zeta means \mathbb{P}(\xi\le s)\ge\mathbb{P}(\zeta\le s) for every s\in\mathbb{R}; and (iv) R(\xi+t)=R(\xi)+t.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The four axioms are subadditivity, degree-one positive homogeneity, monotonicity with respect to first-order stochastic dominance, and translation invariance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(\xi+\zeta)\le R(\xi)+R(\zeta),\quad R(\lambda\xi)=\lambda R(\xi),\quad \xi\preccurlyeq\zeta\Rightarrow R(\xi)\le R(\zeta),\quad R(\xi+t)=R(\xi)+t

knowledge_statements.title: Capital-Requirement Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk as the infimal cash addition making a payoff acceptable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) be an ordered linear space containing the constants, and let \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal X\) be upward closed: if \(X\in\mathcal A\) and \(Y\ge X\), then \(Y\in\mathcal A\). Define \[\rho_{\mathcal A}(X)=\inf\{m\in\mathbb R:X+m\in\mathcal A\},\] where the infimum is taken in \(\overline{\mathbb R}\). Thus \(\rho_{\mathcal A}(X)\) is the required capital in the infimum sense; it is an attained least amount only when the feasible set attains its infimum. For every \(c\in\mathbb R\), \(\rho_{\mathcal A}(X+c)=\rho_{\mathcal A}(X)-c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A payoff's capital requirement is the infimum of the cash amounts that make it acceptable; this need not be an attained minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is an ordered linear space containing all constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathcal A}(X)=\inf\{m\in\mathbb R:X+m\in\mathcal A\}\) and \(\rho_{\mathcal A}(X+c)=\rho_{\mathcal A}(X)-c\).

children.title: Preference Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Ordering of uncertain prospects through risk-sensitive preference comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Preference Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preference ordering represented by a payoff risk functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) be a set of payoffs and let \(\rho:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\). Define \[X\succeq_{\rho}Y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\rho(X)\le\rho(Y).\] Then \(\succeq_{\rho}\) is a complete preorder. If \(\rho\) is decreasing with respect to the payoff order, then \(X\ge Y\) implies \(X\succeq_{\rho}Y\). If \(\mathcal X\) is closed under addition of constants and \(\rho(X+m)=\rho(X)-m\) for every admissible \(X\) and \(m\in\mathbb R\), then adding the same constant to both alternatives leaves their comparison unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A payoff is weakly preferred exactly when its assessed risk is no greater. If the risk functional is cash additive in the payoff convention, adding the same cash amount to both alternatives preserves their comparison.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is a set of payoffs.

children.title: Certainty-Equivalent Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Deterministic-value interpretation of evaluations assigned to uncertain prospects.

knowledge_statements.title: Certainty-Equivalent Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certain payoff indifferent to a specified random payoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\succeq\) be a complete preorder on a set \(\mathcal X\) containing every constant random variable, and define \(X\sim Y\) by \(X\succeq Y\) and \(Y\succeq X\). A certainty equivalent of \(X\in\mathcal X\) is a number \(c(X)\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \[X\sim c(X).\] If constants are strictly ordered and a certainty equivalent exists for every \(X\in\mathcal X\), then it is unique and \(X\succeq Y\) if and only if \(c(X)\ge c(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certainty equivalent is a certain amount indifferent to the payoff. It is unique and represents the preference ordering when preferences form a complete preorder, constants are strictly ordered, and such an amount exists for every payoff.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) contains every constant random variable.
\(\succeq\) is a complete preorder on \(\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A certainty equivalent satisfies \(X\sim c(X)\); under strict ordering of constants and existence for every payoff, it is unique and \(X\succeq Y\Longleftrightarrow c(X)\ge c(Y)\).

notation.meaning: indifference relation induced by the preorder

children.title: Preference–Certainty-Equivalent Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Compatibility and translation boundaries between preference orderings and certainty-equivalent evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Preference–Certainty-Equivalent Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence among cash-additive certainty equivalents, represented preferences, and normalized payoff risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) contain the constants and be closed under their addition. Suppose \(c:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \(c(m)=m\) for every \(m\in\mathbb R\) and \(c(X+m)=c(X)+m\). Define \(X\succeq Y\) by \(c(X)\ge c(Y)\), and set \(\rho(X)=-c(X)\). Then \(X\succeq Y\) if and only if \(\rho(X)\le\rho(Y)\), \(X\sim c(X)\), \(\rho(0)=0\), and \(\rho(X+m)=\rho(X)-m\). Conversely, if \(\rho:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is normalized and satisfies this cash-translation rule, then \(c=-\rho\) has the stated normalization and cash-additivity properties and represents the same induced preference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized cash-additive certainty-equivalent functional and a normalized payoff risk functional are negatives of one another and represent the same induced preferences.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) contains all constants and is closed under addition of constants.
\(c(m)=m\) and \(c(X+m)=c(X)+m\) for every admissible \(X\) and \(m\in\mathbb R\).

knowledge_statements.title: Monetary Risk Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss-convention definition on essentially bounded random variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a probability space \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\), a monetary risk measure in the loss convention is a map \(\rho:L^{\infty}\to\mathbb R\) satisfying, for all \(L,M\in L^{\infty}\) and \(m\in\mathbb R\), \[L\le M\ \mathbb P\text{-a.s.}\Rightarrow\rho(L)\le\rho(M),\qquad \rho(L+m)=\rho(L)+m.\] The first condition is monotonicity and the second is cash additivity. If normalization is imposed, it additionally requires \(\rho(0)=0\), which then implies \(\rho(m)=m\) for every constant \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monetary loss risk measure is monotone and cash additive; normalization additionally makes the risk of each constant equal that constant.
assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) is a probability space.

notation.meaning: essentially bounded random losses modulo almost-sure equality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The loss-convention definition is internally correct and fits the container, including the optional normalization convention, but no authoritative risk-measure source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Risk Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diversification-sensitive monetary risk measures in the loss convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex risk measure is a monetary loss risk measure \(\rho:L^{\infty}\to\mathbb R\) that also satisfies, for every \(L,M\in L^{\infty}\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), \[\rho\bigl(\lambda L+(1-\lambda)M\bigr)\le \lambda\rho(L)+(1-\lambda)\rho(M).\] Thus the risk assigned to a diversified loss position does not exceed the corresponding convex combination of stand-alone risks. Normalization \(\rho(0)=0\) is an additional convention unless included in the adopted definition of monetary risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex risk measure is monetary and assigns a mixture no more risk than the same mixture of the component risks.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho:L^{\infty}\to\mathbb R\) is a monetary loss risk measure.

notation.meaning: diversification weight in the unit interval

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and diversification inequality are correct in the stated loss convention, but the record lacks a supporting source with a section, definition, theorem, or page locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual-domain characterization of convex risk-measure axioms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The explicit dual characterizations are retained; the referenced formula (6.36) is not restated because it is absent from the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\rho:\mathcal Z\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper, convex, and lower semicontinuous, and set \(\mathfrak A=\operatorname{dom}\rho^*\). Then monotonicity \((R2)\) holds if and only if every \(\zeta\in\mathfrak A\) is nonnegative almost surely. Translation equivariance \((R3)\) holds if and only if \(\int_\Omega\zeta\,dP=1\) for every \(\zeta\in\mathfrak A\). Positive homogeneity \((R4)\) holds if and only if \(\rho\) is the support function of \(\mathfrak A\), namely \(\rho(Z)=\sup_{\zeta\in\mathfrak A}\langle\zeta,Z\rangle\) for every \(Z\in\mathcal Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous convex risk measure, monotonicity is equivalent to nonnegative elements in the conjugate domain, translation equivariance to all such elements having unit expectation, and positive homogeneity to the risk measure being the support function of that domain.
assumptions_latex: \rho:\mathcal Z\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is proper, convex, and lower semicontinuous}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate and Subdifferential of an Expected Convex-Loss Functional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extract references representation (6.35) without reproducing it, so that representation is retained by label rather than reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper, convex, nondecreasing, and lower semicontinuous. Suppose \(\rho(Z)=\mathbb E[g(Z)]\) is well defined and proper. Then \(\rho\) is convex and lower semicontinuous, satisfies monotonicity condition (R2), and the representation denoted (6.35) holds with \[\rho^*(\zeta)=\mathbb E[g^*(\zeta)].\] Moreover, if \(\rho(Z)\) is finite, then \[\partial\rho(Z)=\{\zeta\in\mathcal Z^*: \zeta(\omega)\in\partial g(Z(\omega))\text{ for }P\text{-almost every }\omega\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The expectation of a proper lower-semicontinuous convex nondecreasing scalar function is a proper convex lower-semicontinuous monotone functional. Its referenced dual representation uses the expected pointwise conjugate, and at finite points its subgradients are characterized pointwise almost everywhere.
assumptions_latex: g:\mathbb R\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is proper, convex, nondecreasing, and lower semicontinuous}
\rho(Z)=\mathbb E[g(Z)]\text{ is well defined and proper}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho\text{ is convex and lower semicontinuous and satisfies (R2); representation (6.35) holds with }\rho^*(\zeta)=\mathbb E[g^*(\zeta)];\quad \rho(Z)<+\infty\Rightarrow\partial\rho(Z)=\{\zeta\in\mathcal Z^*: \zeta(\omega)\in\partial g(Z(\omega))\ P\text{-a.e.}\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdifferential Formula for a Convex Risk Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions (R1) and (R2) remain symbolic because their definitions are absent from the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Z=L_p(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)\), let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathcal Z\) be convex with \([F(x)](\omega)=f_\omega(x)\), and set \(\bar Z=F(\bar x)\). Suppose \(\rho\) satisfies (R1) and (R2), is finite valued, and is continuous at \(\bar Z\). Then \(\phi=\rho\circ F\) is subdifferentiable at \(\bar x\), and \[\partial\phi(\bar x)=\operatorname{cl}\left(\bigcup_{\zeta\in\partial\rho(\bar Z)}\int_\Omega\partial f_\omega(\bar x)\zeta(\omega)\,dP(\omega)\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under conditions (R1) and (R2), finiteness, and continuity at the image point, the composite subdifferential is the closure of the union of the weighted integrals of pointwise subdifferentials.
assumptions_latex: \rho\text{ satisfies (R1) and (R2), is finite valued, and is continuous at }\bar Z
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi=\rho\circ F\text{ is subdifferentiable at }\bar x,\quad \partial\phi(\bar x)=\operatorname{cl}\left(\bigcup_{\zeta\in\partial\rho(\bar Z)}\int_\Omega\partial f_\omega(\bar x)\zeta(\omega)\,dP(\omega)\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity and Pointwise Directional Derivatives of Convex Lp-Valued Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general convex-analysis result for mappings into an Lp space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Z=L_p(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)\), let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathcal Z\) be convex, and write \([F(x)](\omega)=f_\omega(x)\). Then \(F\) is continuous and directionally differentiable, and for every \(\bar x,h\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\omega\in\Omega\), \([F'(\bar x;h)](\omega)=f_\omega'(\bar x;h)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex mapping from finite-dimensional Euclidean space into an Lp space is continuous and directionally differentiable, with its directional derivative given pointwise by the directional derivatives of its scalar realizations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is continuous and directionally differentiable, and }[F'(\bar x;h)](\omega)=f_\omega'(\bar x;h)\quad(\bar x,h\in\mathbb R^n,\ \omega\in\Omega).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Risk-Composition Subdifferential under Scenario Differentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the differentiable-scenario specialization of the preceding composite subdifferential theorem; its assumptions are stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Z=L_p(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)\), let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathcal Z\) be convex with \([F(x)](\omega)=f_\omega(x)\), set \(\bar Z=F(\bar x)\), and suppose \(\rho\) satisfies (R1) and (R2), is finite valued, and is continuous at \(\bar Z\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calculus for a convex functional composed with an Lp-valued convex mapping.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Saddle-point characterization for convex risk optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes saddle points through a risk subgradient and a decision-space stationarity condition; notation follows the referenced primal-dual formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathcal Z is convex and \rho:\mathcal Z\to\overline{\mathbb R} is proper, lower semicontinuous, and satisfies (R1)--(R2). knowledge_statements.title: Coherent Risk Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positively homogeneous, subadditive monetary risk in the loss convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coherent risk measure is a monetary loss risk measure \(\rho:L^{\infty}\to\mathbb R\) that is subadditive and positively homogeneous: for all \(L,M\in L^{\infty}\) and \(t\ge0\), \[\rho(L+M)\le\rho(L)+\rho(M),\qquad \rho(tL)=t\rho(L).\] Together with monotonicity and cash additivity, these axioms imply \(\rho(0)=0\) and convexity. Subadditivity formalizes diversification, while positive homogeneity makes risk scale linearly with position size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coherent risk measure is monetary, subadditive, and positively homogeneous; these axioms also imply normalization and convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho:L^{\infty}\to\mathbb R\) is a monetary loss risk measure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coherent-risk axioms and their stated normalization and convexity consequences are correct for a finite-valued monetary loss risk measure, but no authoritative source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kusuoka representation of law-invariant coherent risk measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static representation on a nonatomic probability space as a supremum of mixtures of average value-at-risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,P)\) be nonatomic and let \(\rho:\mathcal Z\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be a law-invariant, lower-semicontinuous coherent risk measure. Then there exists a set \(\mathfrak M\) of probability measures on \((0,1]\), equipped with its Borel sigma-algebra, such that \[\rho(Z)=\sup_{\mu\in\mathfrak M}\int_0^1\operatorname{AV@R}_{\alpha}(Z)\,d\mu(\alpha),\qquad \forall Z\in\mathcal Z.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a nonatomic probability space, every law-invariant lower-semicontinuous coherent risk measure has a representation as the supremum of probability mixtures of average value-at-risk.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho:\mathcal Z\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is coherent, law invariant, and lower semicontinuous.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Law invariance and finite-space degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines law invariance relative to a reference probability measure and records a finite-space condition under which it becomes automatic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A risk measure \(\rho:\mathcal Z\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is law invariant with respect to \(P\) if, for every \(Z_1,Z_2\in\mathcal Z\), \(Z_1\overset{\mathcal D}{\sim}Z_2\Rightarrow \rho(Z_1)=\rho(Z_2)\). If \(\Omega=\{\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_K\}\) has probabilities \(p_1,\ldots,p_K\) satisfying \(\sum_{k\in A}p_k=\sum_{k\in B}p_k\iff A=B\) for all \(A,B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}\), then equally distributed real-valued random variables on \(\Omega\) are identical; consequently every risk measure on this space is law invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A risk measure is law invariant when it assigns the same value to random variables having the same distribution. On a finite probability space whose distinct subsets always have distinct total probabilities, equal distributions force pointwise equality, so every risk measure is automatically law invariant.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho:\mathcal Z\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is a risk measure relative to \(P\).
For the finite-space boundary statement, \(\Omega=\{\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_K\}\) and \(\sum_{k\in A}p_k=\sum_{k\in B}p_k\iff A=B\) for all subsets \(A,B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z_1\overset{\mathcal D}{\sim}Z_2\Rightarrow\rho(Z_1)=\rho(Z_2);\quad\text{under the finite-space condition, }Z_1\overset{\mathcal D}{\sim}Z_2\Rightarrow Z_1=Z_2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proper coherent risk measures for costs and rewards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static risk measures on finite-moment random variables, with both cost and reward sign conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Z=L_p(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)\), \(1\le p<\infty\), with random variables identified up to \(P\)-almost-sure equality. A risk measure \(\rho:\mathcal Z\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper when \(\rho(Z)>-\infty\) for every \(Z\in\mathcal Z\) and \(\operatorname{dom}\rho=\{Z:\rho(Z)<+\infty\}\ne\varnothing\). For random costs, \(\rho\) is coherent when it satisfies convexity, monotonicity \(Z\ge Z'\text{ a.s.}\Rightarrow\rho(Z)\ge\rho(Z')\), translation equivariance \(\rho(Z+a)=\rho(Z)+a\), and positive homogeneity \(\rho(tZ)=t\rho(Z)\) for \(t>0\). For rewards, \(\varrho(Z)=\rho(-Z)\) remains convex and positively homogeneous but satisfies \(Z\ge Z'\text{ a.s.}\Rightarrow\varrho(Z)\le\varrho(Z')\) and \(\varrho(Z+a)=\varrho(Z)-a\). Average Value-at-Risk is coherent and is finite-valued on \(L_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper risk measure for random costs is coherent when it is convex, monotone increasing in cost, translation equivariant, and positively homogeneous. Negating the argument gives the reward convention, reversing the monotonicity and translation signs. Average Value-at-Risk is a finite-valued coherent risk measure on L1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho\text{ is coherent precisely when }(R1)\text{--}(R4)\text{ hold; for }\varrho(Z)=\rho(-Z),\ (R2),(R3)\text{ are replaced by }(R2a),(R3a).

knowledge_statements.title: Law-Invariant Risk Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk functionals depending only on the loss distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho:\mathcal X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be a risk functional on a class of random losses. It is law invariant if, whenever \(L,M\in\mathcal X\) have the same distribution under \(\mathbb P\), \[L\overset{d}{=}M\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\rho(L)=\rho(M).\] Equivalently, there exists a functional \(R\) on the set of probability laws generated by \(\mathcal X\) such that \(\rho(L)=R(\mathcal L(L))\) for every \(L\in\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A law-invariant risk measure assigns equal risk to losses having the same probability distribution, regardless of their realization mechanism.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is a class of random losses on a fixed probability space.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The law-invariance definition and factorization through generated probability laws fit the container, but neither claim has an inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Comonotone Risk Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk measures additive on losses moving in the same statewise direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two random losses \(L,M\) are comonotone if \((L(\omega)-L(\omega'))(M(\omega)-M(\omega'))\ge0\) for \(\mathbb P\otimes\mathbb P\)-almost every \((\omega,\omega')\). A risk measure \(\rho:\mathcal X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is comonotone additive if every comonotone pair \(L,M\in\mathcal X\) with \(L+M\in\mathcal X\) satisfies \[\rho(L+M)=\rho(L)+\rho(M).\] A comonotone risk measure here means a risk measure possessing this additivity property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A comonotone risk measure is additive for losses that move in the same direction across states and therefore provide no diversification.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is closed under addition for the pairs under consideration.

notation.meaning: product probability measure on pairs of states
risk measure on the loss class

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additivity formula is standard, but the label “comonotone risk measure” and the product-almost-everywhere definition of comonotonicity require an authoritative source specifying the adopted convention.

children.title: Comonotone Additivity within Law-Invariant Classes
children.top_down_role: Intersection of distributional invariance with comonotone aggregation structure.

assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) is atomless and \(X,Y\in L^\infty\) are interpreted as losses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comonotone additivity is stated as an additional property; law invariance alone does not imply it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Random losses \(X\) and \(Y\) are comonotone when \((X(\omega)-X(\omega'))(Y(\omega)-Y(\omega'))\geq 0\) for almost every \((\omega,\omega')\). A law-invariant risk functional \(\rho\) is comonotone additive precisely when \(\rho(X+Y)=\rho(X)+\rho(Y)\) for every such pair. In particular, every spectral functional \(\rho_\phi(X)=\int_0^1F_X^{-1}(u)\phi(u)\,du\), where \(\phi\geq0\) and \(\int_0^1\phi(u)\,du=1\), has this property because comonotone sums satisfy \(F_{X+Y}^{-1}=F_X^{-1}+F_Y^{-1}\) almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Comonotone additivity requires the risk of two similarly ordered losses to equal the sum of their risks; spectral risk measures satisfy this property.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss convention with translation equivariance \(\mathcal R(X+c)=\mathcal R(X)+c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal D(X)=\mathcal R(X)-\mathbb E[X]\). Then \(\mathcal D(X+c)=\mathcal D(X)\) for every constant \(c\), \(\mathcal D(0)=0\), and the inverse correspondence is \(\mathcal R(X)=\mathbb E[X]+\mathcal D(X)\). Convexity and positive homogeneity pass between \(\mathcal R\) and \(\mathcal D\). Moreover, \(\mathcal R\) is monotone in the loss order if and only if \(\mathcal D(X)-\mathcal D(Y)\leq\mathbb E[Y-X]\) for every \(X,Y\in L^1\) satisfying \(X\leq Y\) almost surely.

Risk monotonicity corresponds exactly to a pairwise bound on changes in the deviation.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Measure Continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential norm continuity on a normed function space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The risk functional \(\rho\) is continuous at \(X\in\mathcal X\) when \(\rho(X)\in\mathbb R\) and, for every sequence \((X_n)\subset\mathcal X\), \(\|X_n-X\|_{\mathcal X}\to0\) implies \(\rho(X_n)\to\rho(X)\). It is continuous on \(\mathcal X\) when it is finite-valued and continuous at every \(X\in\mathcal X\). Continuity on \(\operatorname{dom}\rho\) may instead be considered with the relative topology and must be identified explicitly as relative continuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A risk functional is norm-continuous at a finite-valued point when norm convergence of losses forces convergence of their risk values; continuity on the whole loss space additionally requires finite values everywhere.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Measure Lower Semicontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological lower semicontinuity, specialized to sequences when the topology is metrizable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The risk functional \(\rho\) is lower semicontinuous at \(X\in\mathcal X\) if every net \((X_\alpha)\) converging to \(X\) in \(\tau\) satisfies \(\rho(X)\leq\liminf_\alpha\rho(X_\alpha)\). When \(\tau\) is metrizable, this is equivalent to requiring \(\rho(X)\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}\rho(X_n)\) whenever \(X_n\to X\). Equivalently, each sublevel set \(\{X\in\mathcal X:\rho(X)\leq a\}\) is \(\tau\)-closed for every \(a\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower semicontinuity prevents the risk at a topological limit from exceeding the limiting inferior risk values and is equivalent to closed sublevel sets; sequences suffice in metrizable topologies.

children.title: Continuity Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Domain, topology, and tail-behavior regimes where stronger continuity properties break down.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Norm continuity does not imply order continuity on \(L^\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates norm continuity from bounded almost-sure, or Lebesgue, continuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho(X)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}X\). Then \(|\rho(X)-\rho(Y)|\leq\|X-Y\|_\infty\), so \(\rho\) is norm-continuous on \(L^\infty\). Choose decreasing measurable sets \(A_n\) with \(\mathbb P(A_n)>0\) and \(\mathbb P(A_n)\downarrow0\), and set \(X_n=\mathbf 1_{A_n}\). Although \(X_n\to0\) almost surely and \(|X_n|\leq1\), one has \(\rho(X_n)=1\) for every \(n\), whereas \(\rho(0)=0\). Hence bounded almost-sure convergence need not imply convergence of risk values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case loss is continuous in the supremum norm but can fail continuity under bounded almost-sure convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuity Failure Boundaries

children.title: Risk-Measure Subdifferentials
children.top_down_role: Set-valued local sensitivity structure for nonsmooth risk functionals.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is a Banach space of losses with continuous dual \(\mathcal X^*\).
\(\rho:\mathcal X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex, and \(X\in\operatorname{dom}\rho\).

notation.meaning: continuous dual of the loss space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-analytic subdifferential in the continuous dual of the loss space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The subdifferential of \(\rho\) at \(X\) is \(\partial\rho(X)=\{Z\in\mathcal X^*: \rho(Y)\geq\rho(X)+\langle Z,Y-X\rangle\ \text{for every }Y\in\mathcal X\}\). Each \(Z\in\partial\rho(X)\) supplies a globally valid affine lower support to \(\rho\). If \(\rho\) is translation equivariant and constants belong to \(\mathcal X\), then every subgradient satisfies \(\langle Z,\mathbf1\rangle=1\). If \(\rho\) is also monotone for the loss order, its subgradients are positive functionals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A risk subgradient is a continuous dual element whose affine approximation globally underestimates the convex risk functional.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Measure Subdifferentials

children.title: Risk-Measure Directional Behavior
children.top_down_role: One-sided local variation of risk functionals along admissible directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Measure Directional Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided directional behavior of a proper convex risk functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t>0\), define \(q(t)=(\rho(X+tH)-\rho(X))/t\). Convexity makes \(q(t)\) nondecreasing as \(t\) increases, so the one-sided limit \(\rho'(X;H)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}q(t)=\inf_{t>0}q(t)\) exists in \([ -\infty,+\infty]\). If the mapping \(H\mapsto\rho'(X;H)\) never takes \(-\infty\) and is not identically \(+\infty\), it is positively homogeneous and subadditive, and hence is a proper sublinear functional describing the first-order convex response of risk to perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper convex risk functional has an extended-real one-sided directional derivative obtained from monotone difference quotients; when proper as a function of direction, that derivative is sublinear.

children.title: Subgradient–Direction Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural links between subgradient information and directional sensitivity.

assumptions_latex: \(\rho:\mathcal X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, and is finite and continuous near \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional support-function formula under local continuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Local continuity ensures that \(\partial\rho(X)\) is nonempty and compact. For every direction \(H\in\mathcal X\), the directional derivative equals the support function of this subdifferential: \(\rho'(X;H)=\max_{Z\in\partial\rho(X)}\langle Z,H\rangle\). Consequently, every subgradient gives the lower directional estimate \(\langle Z,H\rangle\leq\rho'(X;H)\), and at least one subgradient attains equality for each fixed direction. If \(\partial\rho(X)=\{Z_X\}\), then \(\rho\) is differentiable at \(X\) with derivative \(Z_X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The directional derivative of a finite-dimensional convex risk functional is the support function of its subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient–Direction Correspondence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-based regimes distinguished by finiteness of the risk functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\leq p<\infty\), the \(L^p\)-integrability condition is \(\mathbb E[|X|^p]<\infty\); for \(p=\infty\), it is \(\operatorname*{ess\,sup}|X|<\infty\). A risk functional operates in the finite-valued \(L^p\) regime when \(\rho:L^p\to\mathbb R\). It operates in an extended-valued regime when \(\rho:L^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), with effective domain \(\operatorname{dom}\rho=\{X\in L^p:\rho(X)<+\infty\}\). Any formula involving \(\mathbb E[X]\) additionally requires \(X\in L^1\), which is automatic for \(p\geq1\) on a probability space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integrability regime specifies the moment space containing losses and whether risk is finite everywhere or only on an effective domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lebesgue-space domain hierarchy and its natural dual pairing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a probability space, \(L^\infty\subseteq L^q\subseteq L^p\subseteq L^1\) continuously whenever \(1\leq p\leq q\leq\infty\). Choosing \(L^p\) as the domain determines both the admissible loss tails and the natural dual pairing: for \(1\leq p<\infty\), continuous linear evaluations have the form \(X\mapsto\mathbb E[ZX]\) with \(Z\in L^{p^*}\), where \(1/p+1/p^*=1\). For \(p=\infty\), the full norm dual is larger than \(L^1\), so restricting dual variables to countably additive densities is an additional modeling choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lebesgue loss domains form nested spaces, and the chosen domain controls admissible tails and the dual variables used to represent risk.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Measure Function-Space Domains

children.title: Domain Extension Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on extending risk functionals across larger or differently topologized spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Extension Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the dual-integrability obstruction to extending risk measures from bounded variables to \(L^p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,P)\) be a probability space, let \(1\le p<\infty\), and let \(q\) be conjugate to \(p\). For a probability measure \(Q\ll P\) with density \(Z=dQ/dP\), the functional \(X\mapsto E_Q[-X]=-E_P[XZ]\) is finite and continuous on \(L^p(P)\) whenever \(Z\in L^q(P)\). If \(Z\notin L^q(P)\), there exists \(X\in L^p(P)\) for which \(E_P[|XZ|]=\infty\); hence any dual risk representation involving that \(Q\) cannot define a finite continuous extension to all of \(L^p(P)\) without restricting its dual domain or permitting extended-real values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extension to all of Lp requires dual probability densities to have conjugate integrability; otherwise some Lp positions have undefined or infinite dual expectations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z\in L^q(P)\) is the continuity regime; if \(Z\notin L^q(P)\), finiteness on every \(X\in L^p(P)\) can fail.

notation.meaning: Space of p-integrable random variables modulo almost-sure equality
Radon–Nikodym density of Q relative to P

knowledge_statements.title: Acceptance-Set Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates monetary-risk axioms to geometric properties of the zero-capital acceptance set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be an ordered vector space of real random variables containing constants, and let \(\rho:L\to(-\infty,\infty]\) satisfy cash additivity \(\rho(X+m)=\rho(X)-m\). Define \(A_\rho=\{X\in L:\rho(X)\le0\}\). If \(\rho\) is monotone, then \(A_\rho+L_+\subseteq A_\rho\). If \(\rho\) is convex, then \(A_\rho\) is convex. If \(\rho\) is positively homogeneous in addition to convexity, then \(A_\rho\) is a convex cone. Thus monotonicity, convexity, and coherence induce upper-set, convex-set, and convex-cone geometry, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The acceptance set of a monetary risk measure is upward closed; convexity makes it convex, and positive homogeneity makes it a convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho\) monotone implies \(A_\rho+L_+\subseteq A_\rho\); convexity and positive homogeneity yield the stated additional geometry.

notation.meaning: Acceptance set induced by the risk measure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated upper-set, convex-set, and convex-cone implications fit the container and are mathematically standard, but the record has no inspectable citation or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Capital-Requirement Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovers a monetary risk measure as the least deterministic capital making a position acceptable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) contain all constant random variables and let \(A\subseteq L\) be nonempty, proper, and monotone, meaning \(A+L_+\subseteq A\). Define the capital requirement by \[\rho_A(X)=\inf\{m\in\mathbb R:X+m\in A\},\] with the infimum taken in the extended real line. Then \(\rho_A\) is monotone and cash additive: \(\rho_A(X+c)=\rho_A(X)-c\). If \(A=A_\rho=\{X:\rho(X)\le0\}\) for a finite-valued monetary risk measure \(\rho\), then \(\rho_{A_\rho}(X)=\rho(X)\) for every \(X\in L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monetary risk measure equals the least cash amount that moves a position into its acceptance set.
assumptions_latex: \(A\subseteq L\) is nonempty, proper, and satisfies \(A+L_+\subseteq A\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_A(X)=\inf\{m\in\mathbb R:X+m\in A\}\), and \(\rho_{A_\rho}=\rho\) for finite-valued monetary \(\rho\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The capital-requirement formula and finite-valued recovery claim fit the terminal container, but no authoritative acceptance-set representation source or locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceptance-Set Closure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States when acceptance-set recovery returns the original set rather than only a closure enlargement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L	o\mathbb R\) carry a topology for which addition of constants is continuous, and let \(A\subseteq L\) be monotone and satisfy \(A+\mathbb R_+\subseteq A\). For \(\rho_A(X)=\inf\{m\in\mathbb R:X+m\in A\}\), its induced acceptance set obeys \[A\subseteq A_{\rho_A}:=\{X:\rho_A(X)\le0\}\subseteq\overline A.\] Consequently, closedness of \(A\) implies \(A_{\rho_A}=A\). Without closedness, boundary positions approachable by arbitrarily small capital additions may belong to \(A_{\rho_A}\setminus A\), so capital-requirement recovery need not preserve the original acceptance set exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovering an acceptance set from its capital requirement yields a set between the original set and its closure; exact recovery follows from closedness.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is monotone and stable under addition of nonnegative constants
Addition of constants is continuous in the topology on \(L\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\subseteq A_{\rho_A}\subseteq\overline A\); in particular, closed \(A\) satisfies \(A_{\rho_A}=A\).

notation.meaning: Acceptance set induced by the recovered capital requirement
