children.title: Separable Optimality Conditions
children.top_down_role: Optimality structure arising from decomposable probabilistic constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Optimality Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient convex KKT conditions for separable objectives coupled by one linear equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(i=1,\ldots,N\), let \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(f_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(A_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^p\) be linear. Consider
\[
\min_{x_i\in C_i}\ \sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{i=1}^N A_i x_i=b,
\]
where \(b\in\mathbb R^p\). Assume the problem has a feasible point with finite objective value and
\[
b\in\operatorname{ri}\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^N A_i(\operatorname{dom}f_i\cap C_i)\right).
\]
Then a feasible point \(x^*=(x_i^*)_{i=1}^N\) is optimal if and only if there exists \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R^p\) such that
\[
0\in\partial f_i(x_i^*)+A_i^{\mathsf T}\lambda^*+N_{C_i}(x_i^*)\quad(i=1,\ldots,N),
\qquad \sum_{i=1}^N A_i x_i^*=b.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a relative-interior constraint qualification, a feasible separable convex point is optimal exactly when one coupling multiplier makes every block stationary over its local feasible set.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and each \(f_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
The problem has a feasible point with finite objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal feasibility and the displayed blockwise stationarity inclusions are necessary and sufficient for optimality.

notation.meaning: convex normal cone to the local feasible set
convex subdifferential of the block objective

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary and sufficient optimality certificate for the reduced separable problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes optimal solutions of problem (4.42) through an active point, a finite convex combination of vectors from $V(u)$, and the orthant normal cone.

Assume that constraint qualification (4.45) holds and that $X$ is compact. A vector $u\geq0$ is an optimal solution of problem (4.42) if and only if there exist $x\in X(u)$, vectors $v^1,\ldots,v^{m+1}\in V(u)$, and scalars $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{m+1}\geq0$ such that $\sum_{j=1}^{m+1}\beta_j=1$ and
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{m+1}\beta_jv^j-g(x)\in\mathcal N_{\mathbb R_+^m}(u).
\]

children.title: Separable Dual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Dual objects and certificates associated with separable chance-constrained structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Dual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coupling multiplier and attained block minima certify global primal and dual optimality through zero duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(i=1,ots,N\), let \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), let \(f_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(A_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^p\) be linear, and let \(b\in\mathbb R^p\). Consider the primal problem
\[
\min_{x_i\in C_i}\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{i=1}^N A_i x_i=b
\]
and define its dual function by
\[
q(\lambda)=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_{i=1}^N\inf_{x_i\in C_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_i x_i\bigr),\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R^p.
\]
Suppose \(x^*=(x_i^*)_{i=1}^N\) satisfies \(x_i^*\in C_i\), \(\sum_{i=1}^N A_i x_i^*=b\), and, for some \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R^p\),
\[
x_i^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in C_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+(\lambda^*)^{\mathsf T}A_i x_i\bigr)\quad(i=1,\ldots,N).
\]
Then \(\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i^*)=q(\lambda^*)\). By weak duality, \(x^*\) is primal optimal and \(\lambda^*\) is dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible collection of blocks and a common multiplier certify global optimality when every block minimizes its Lagrangian term, because their primal-dual gap is then zero.
assumptions_latex: The displayed primal and dual functions are well-defined.
The assembled point satisfies \(x_i^*\in C_i\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^N A_i x_i^*=b\).
Each \(x_i^*\) attains the displayed blockwise Lagrangian minimum at \(\lambda^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i^*)=q(\lambda^*)\), so \(x^*\) and \(\lambda^*\) are primal and dual optimal.

children.title: Primal–Dual Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between separable primal components and their dual counterparts.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual subgradient decomposition of a convex separable program with linear coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\lambda^0\), positive steps \(\gamma_k\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), repeat for \(k=0,1,\ldots\): independently compute
\[
x_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in C_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+(\lambda^k)^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i\bigr),\qquad i=1,\ldots,N,
\]
form the coupling residual \(r^k=\sum_iA_ix_i^k-b\), and update \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\gamma_k r^k\). Stop when a primal recovery \(\hat x^k\) is feasible and its computable primal-dual gap relative to \(q(\lambda^k)\) is at most \(\varepsilon\); output \((\hat x^k,\lambda^k)\). With \(\sum_k\gamma_k=\infty\), \(\sum_k\gamma_k^2<\infty\), bounded subgradients, and dual attainment, the dual values converge to the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve local Lagrangian blocks in parallel, update the coupling multiplier by their aggregate residual, and stop with a feasible small-gap primal recovery.
assumptions_latex: The block objectives and sets are convex, and every stated block minimization is attained.
Dual optimal solutions exist and the generated dual subgradients are bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration decomposes across blocks, and under the stated assumptions \(q(\lambda^k)\) converges to the optimal dual value.

children.title: Duality-Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regularity regimes governing exact or inexact primal–dual correspondence.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies the separable convex primal–dual gap under a coupling equality and a relative-interior qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_1,\ldots,E_m\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(A_i:E_i\to Y\) be linear, let \(b\in Y\), and let \(h_i=f_i+\delta_{X_i}:E_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). Define \(P=\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^m h_i(x_i):\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\}\) and \(D=\sup_{y\in Y}\{-\langle y,b\rangle+\sum_{i=1}^m\inf_{x_i\in E_i}(h_i(x_i)+\langle y,A_i x_i\rangle)\}\). Weak duality gives \(D\le P\). If every \(h_i\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(P\in\mathbb R\), and \(b\in\operatorname{ri}(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i\operatorname{dom}h_i)\), then \(D=P\). Without this qualification, a finite primal value can have either a positive finite gap or \(D=-\infty\), corresponding respectively to a positive or infinite extended gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak duality always bounds the dual value by the primal value. For proper closed convex data, a finite primal value and the stated relative-interior qualification give zero gap; without the qualification, a finite primal value may have a positive or infinite gap.
assumptions_latex: \(E_i\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces, \(A_i:E_i\to Y\) is linear, and \(b\in Y\).
\(h_i=f_i+\delta_{X_i}\) is proper, closed, and convex for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=P\) under the stated qualification, while universally \(D\le P\).

notation.meaning: Extended-real local objective incorporating the local feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Scalar Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar reformulation when feasibility is a threshold event in a monotone uncertain variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi\) be scalar with distribution function \(F\), let \(0<\varepsilon<1\), and suppose that for every decision \(x\) there is a threshold \(\tau(x)\) such that \(g(x,\xi)\le0\) holds exactly when \(\xi\le\tau(x)\). Then \(\mathbb P(g(x,\xi)\le0)=F(\tau(x))\), so the chance constraint is equivalent to \(F(\tau(x))\ge1-\varepsilon\). With the left quantile \(q_p=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:F(t)\ge p\}\), right-continuity of \(F\) gives the deterministic form \(\tau(x)\ge q_{1-\varepsilon}\).

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Quantile Constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Distribution-Function Inversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized inverse identities used in exact scalar chance-constraint reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a distribution function \(F\), define \(q_p=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:F(t)\ge p\}\) for \(p\in(0,1)\). Then right-continuity and monotonicity imply \(F(t)\ge p\) if and only if \(t\ge q_p\). Consequently, every scalar threshold constraint \(F(\tau(x))\ge p\) is equivalent to \(\tau(x)\ge q_p\). If \(F\) is continuous and strictly increasing on its effective support, then \(q_p=F^{-1}(p)\) and \(F(q_p)=p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generalized quantile converts a distribution-function inequality into a threshold inequality; for continuous strictly increasing distributions it is the ordinary inverse.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a distribution function on \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(t)\ge p\iff t\ge q_p\), with \(q_p=F^{-1}(p)\) when \(F\) is continuous and strictly increasing.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Gaussian Individual Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic equivalent of one affine individual chance constraint under multivariate Gaussian uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi\sim\mathcal N(\mu,\Sigma)\) and \(g(x,\xi)=\alpha(x)+\beta(x)^{\mathsf T}\xi\). The scalar \(g(x,\xi)\) is Gaussian with mean \(m(x)=\alpha(x)+\beta(x)^{\mathsf T}\mu\) and standard deviation \(s(x)=\|\Sigma^{1/2}\beta(x)\|_2\). Hence, for \(0<\varepsilon<1\), the individual constraint \(\mathbb P(g(x,\xi)\le0)\ge1-\varepsilon\) is equivalent to \(m(x)+\Phi^{-1}(1-\varepsilon)s(x)\le0\), including the deterministic case \(s(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gaussian affine chance constraint equals a mean bound plus the standard deviation multiplied by the required standard-normal quantile.

notation.meaning: Mean and standard deviation of the affine random constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Cone Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic representation of an affine Gaussian individual constraint at reliability at least one half.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\alpha(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x-d\), \(\beta(x)=Bx+e\), and \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\). Set \(\kappa=\Phi^{-1}(1-\varepsilon)\ge0\). Projection onto \(x\) yields precisely the original individual chance-constrained feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With affine coefficients and reliability at least one half, the Gaussian quantile reformulation is represented by one norm cone and one linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\alpha(x)+\beta(x)^{\mathsf T}\xi\le0)\ge1-\varepsilon\) is the projection of the displayed second-order-cone system.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gaussian individual chance constraints as SOC constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact SOCP reformulation of individual linear chance constraints with normally distributed coefficient vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x c^\top x\) subject to \(\mathbb P(a_i^\top x\le b_i)\ge p_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\). If \(p_i>1/2\) and the \(a_i\) are independent Gaussian vectors with means \(\bar a_i\) and covariance matrices \(\Sigma_i\succ0\), then the problem is equivalent to the SOCP \[\min_x c^\top x\quad\text{s.t.}\quad \bar a_i^\top x+\Phi^{-1}(p_i)\|\Sigma_i^{1/2}x\|_2\le b_i,\quad i=1,\ldots,m,\] where \(\Phi^{-1}\) is the standard-normal quantile function.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint-Gaussian Probability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating exact multivariate-normal evaluation from marginal or conic individual reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi\sim\mathcal N(\mu,\Sigma)\), let \(Y=A\xi\), and write \(V=A\Sigma A^{\mathsf T}\). The joint constraint \(\mathbb P(A\xi\le b(x))\ge1-\varepsilon\) is exactly \(\Phi_m(b(x)-A\mu;V)\ge1-\varepsilon\), where inequalities are componentwise. Its probability boundary is \(\Phi_m(b(x)-A\mu;V)=1-\varepsilon\). Separate marginal quantile constraints do not describe this boundary in general because dependence enters through \(V\); allocating risks \(\varepsilon_j\) with \(\sum_j\varepsilon_j\le\varepsilon\) gives a Bonferroni sufficient condition, not a generally exact reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint Gaussian feasibility is a multivariate-normal probability boundary. Separate Gaussian quantiles generally provide only risk-allocation approximations because correlation couples the events.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and inequalities are componentwise.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Selection Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact subset-selection form of a chance constraint for a finite probability distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the uncertainty have scenarios \(s=1,\ldots,N\) with probabilities \(p_s>0\) satisfying \(\sum_s p_s=1\), and let \(g_s(x)\le0\) denote feasibility in scenario \(s\). Then \(\mathbb P(g(x,\xi)\le0)\ge1-\varepsilon\) holds if and only if there exists a selected set \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\) such that \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s\ge1-\varepsilon\) and \(g_s(x)\le0\) for every \(s\in S\). Thus the feasible region is a union over all sufficiently probable scenario subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite uncertainty, chance feasibility means satisfying every constraint in at least one selected scenario subset whose total probability reaches the reliability target.

notation.meaning: Selected subset of scenarios enforced by the decision.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixing Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A canonical valid inequality strengthening the relaxation of a binary mixing set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the mixing set \(Q=\{(y,z):y\ge h_i(1-z_i)\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,n,\ y\ge0,\ z\in\{0,1\}^n\}\), with \(h_1\ge h_2\ge\cdots\ge h_n\ge0\), and define \(h_{n+1}=0\). Every point of \(Q\) satisfies the mixing inequality \(y+\sum_{i=1}^n(h_i-h_{i+1})z_i\ge h_1\). Adding this inequality to the continuous relaxation couples the indicator variables and dominates retaining only the separate bounds \(y\ge h_i(1-z_i)\) for fractional \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordered binary on-off lower bounds imply one aggregate mixing inequality that couples the indicators and strengthens their continuous relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cover Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid cover cuts for the weighted violation-budget constraint in finite-support chance formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_s\in\{0,1\}\) indicate scenario violations and suppose \(\sum_{s=1}^N p_s z_s\le\varepsilon\), with \(p_s>0\). A set \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\) is a cover when \(\sum_{s\in C}p_s>\varepsilon\). Since all indicators in a cover cannot simultaneously equal one, every feasible vector satisfies \(\sum_{s\in C}z_s\le|C|-1\). If \(C\) is minimal, meaning removal of any member destroys the cover property, the inequality is undominated by cover inequalities obtained from proper subsets of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any scenario set whose probability exceeds the violation budget cannot be entirely discarded, yielding a valid binary cover inequality.

notation.meaning: A cover for the violation-probability budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Inequality Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential lifting of a valid inequality from a binary face to the full finite-scenario polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\{0,1\}^{n+k}\), write its variables as \((x,z)\), and suppose \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is valid on \(P\cap\{z=0\}\). For a lifting order \(1,\ldots,k\), define recursively
\[\alpha_j=b-\max\left\{a^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{i<j}\alpha_i z_i:(x,z)\in P,\ z_j=1,\ z_i=0\ \text{for }i>j\right\}.\]
Whenever each displayed maximum is finite and its feasible set is nonempty, the sequentially lifted inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{j=1}^k\alpha_jz_j\le b\) is valid for \(P\). Different lifting orders may produce different valid coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential lifting computes each new binary-variable coefficient by residual maximization. The resulting inequality is valid for the full polytope, although its coefficients can depend on the lifting order.
assumptions_latex: Every lifting subproblem has a finite attained maximum.

notation.meaning: Binary variable introduced at lifting step j.

children.title: Facet-Strength Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Facet-Strength Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension test separating facet-defining inequalities from lower-dimensional valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a polytope of affine dimension \(d\ge 1\), and let \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) be valid for \(P\). Define \(F=\{x\in P:a^{\mathsf T}x=b\}\), and assume that \(F\) is nonempty and proper, meaning \(F\ne P\). Then \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is facet-defining for \(P\) if and only if \(\dim(F)=d-1\). Under the proper-face assumption, this is equivalent to \(F\) containing \(d\) affinely independent points. If \(\dim(F)<d-1\), the inequality does not define a facet.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid inequality whose tight set is a nonempty proper face is facet-defining exactly when that face has dimension one less than the polytope, equivalently when it contains d affinely independent points.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a polytope with affine dimension \(d\ge1\).
\(F=\{x\in P:a^{\mathsf T}x=b\}\) is nonempty and satisfies \(F\ne P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) defines a facet of \(P\) if and only if \(\dim(F)=d-1\), equivalently if and only if \(F\) contains \(d\) affinely independent points.

notation.meaning: Proper face on which the inequality is tight.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Support Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scenario decomposition of a finite-support chance constraint using violation indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi\) take values \(\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^S\) with probabilities \(p_s>0\), and set \(g_s(x)=g(x,\xi^s)\). Assume constants \(M_s\ge0\) satisfy \(g_s(x)\le M_s\) for every admissible \(x\). Then
\[\mathbb P\{g(x,\xi)\le0\}\ge1-\varepsilon\]
holds if and only if there exists \(z\in\{0,1\}^S\) such that
\[g_s(x)\le M_sz_s\quad(s=1,\ldots,S),\qquad \sum_{s=1}^Sp_sz_s\le\varepsilon.\]
Thus the finite-support probability constraint decomposes into scenario constraints coupled only through a weighted violation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite distribution, a chance constraint is equivalent to scenario-wise big-M constraints plus a probability-weighted budget on binary violation indicators.
assumptions_latex: \(M_s\) is a valid upper bound for \(g_s\) on the admissible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Component Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product reformulation for componentwise joint chance constraints under mutual independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_m\) be mutually independent real random variables with distribution functions \(F_i\), and let \(b_i:X\to\mathbb R\). For every \(x\in X\),
\[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{\xi_i\le b_i(x)\}\right)=\prod_{i=1}^m F_i(b_i(x)).\]
Consequently, the joint chance constraint
\[\mathbb P\!\left(\xi_i\le b_i(x)\ \text{for all }i\right)\ge1-\varepsilon\]
is exactly equivalent to \(\prod_{i=1}^mF_i(b_i(x))\ge1-\varepsilon\). No continuity assumption on the marginal distributions is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When random components are mutually independent and each constraint uses one component, joint reliability equals the product of marginal satisfaction probabilities.
assumptions_latex: \(b_i(x)\) is a finite threshold for every \(i\) and \(x\).

notation.meaning: Marginal distribution function of component i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: factorization of probabilities for mutually independent events.
A direct probability or chance-constraint source with a specific locator remains required.

knowledge_statements.title: Known-Copula Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact copula evaluation of a componentwise joint chance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_m)\) have marginal distribution functions \(F_1,\ldots,F_m\) and a specified copula \(C\) satisfying
\[\mathbb P(\xi_1\le t_1,\ldots,\xi_m\le t_m)=C(F_1(t_1),\ldots,F_m(t_m)).\]
For measurable finite thresholds \(b_i(x)\), the joint chance constraint is exactly
\[C\!\left(F_1(b_1(x)),\ldots,F_m(b_m(x))\right)\ge1-\varepsilon.\]
If some marginals are discontinuous, the statement presumes that the specified copula is one compatible with the given joint distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a known compatible copula, joint reliability is obtained by applying that copula to the marginal satisfaction probabilities.
assumptions_latex: The joint distribution has specified marginals \(F_i\) and a compatible copula \(C\).
Each \(b_i(x)\) is a measurable finite threshold.

notation.meaning: Specified copula of the random vector.

children.title: Ordered-Event Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Ordered-Event Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tail events generated by totally ordered thresholds of one scalar random variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y\) be a real random variable and let \(t_1\le\cdots\le t_m\). Define upper-tail violation events \(V_i=\{Y>t_i\}\). Then \(V_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq V_m\), and hence
\[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^mV_i\right)=\mathbb P(V_1)=1-F_Y(t_1),\qquad \mathbb P\!\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^mV_i\right)=\mathbb P(V_m)=1-F_Y(t_m).\]
Thus a reliability constraint excluding every violation, \(\mathbb P(\bigcup_iV_i)\le\varepsilon\), reduces exactly to \(1-F_Y(t_1)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordered scalar thresholds create nested tail events, so union and intersection probabilities reduce to the least and most restrictive thresholds.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is a real random variable with distribution function \(F_Y\).

notation.meaning: Upper-tail violation event at threshold i.

children.title: Nested-Event Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Event Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability calculus for an arbitrary finite chain of nested measurable events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E_1,\ldots,E_m\) be measurable events satisfying \(E_1\subseteq E_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq E_m\). Then
\[\bigcup_{i=1}^mE_i=E_m,\qquad \bigcap_{i=1}^mE_i=E_1,\]
and therefore
\[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^mE_i\right)=\mathbb P(E_m)=\max_i\mathbb P(E_i),\qquad \mathbb P\!\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^mE_i\right)=\mathbb P(E_1)=\min_i\mathbb P(E_i).\]
Accordingly, a union-risk bound needs only the maximal event, while a joint-satisfaction bound needs only the minimal event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chain of nested events, the union is the largest event and the intersection is the smallest, eliminating all intermediate probability constraints.

notation.meaning: Event at position i in the inclusion chain.

children.title: Order-to-Nesting Specialization

knowledge_statements.title: Order-to-Nesting Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone scalar thresholds convert a total parameter order into event inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y\) be a real random variable and define \(E(t)=\{Y\le t\}\). If \(t_1\le\cdots\le t_m\), monotonicity of the sublevel sets gives
\[E(t_1)\subseteq E(t_2)\subseteq\cdots\subseteq E(t_m).\]
Consequently,
\[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^mE(t_i)\right)=F_Y(t_1),\qquad \mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^mE(t_i)\right)=F_Y(t_m).\]
More generally, any event family satisfying \(s\le t\Rightarrow E(s)\subseteq E(t)\) converts a total threshold order into the nested-event regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone event map turns ordered thresholds into nested events, permitting exact reduction to an extreme threshold.

children.title: Partial-Order Boundary
children.top_down_role: Dependence structures where only partial ordering is available and nesting fails.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Order Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incomparable events invalidate extreme-event reductions based only on marginal probabilities and inclusion order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(([0,1],\mathcal B,\lambda)\), let \(E_1=[0,1/2]\) and \(E_2=[1/2,1]\). Also let \(E_1'=[0,1/2]\) and \(E_2'=[1/4,3/4]\). In both pairs, neither event contains the other, and every event has probability \(1/2\). Nevertheless,
\[\lambda(E_1\cup E_2)=1,\qquad \lambda(E_1'\cup E_2')=3/4.\]
Thus marginal probabilities together with the same incomparability relation do not determine union risk. Outside an inclusion chain, intersection or dependence information is generally required for an exact reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two pairs of incomparable events can have identical marginal probabilities but different union probabilities, so the extreme-event reduction available for a nested chain does not extend to a partial order.
assumptions_latex: Only event marginal probabilities and inclusion relations are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda(E_i)=\lambda(E_i')=1/2\) for \(i=1,2\), both pairs are incomparable, and \(\lambda(E_1\cup E_2)=1\ne3/4=\lambda(E_1'\cup E_2')\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bonferroni Risk Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence-free sufficient condition for a joint chance constraint via allocated marginal violation probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V_1(x),\ldots,V_m(x)\) be measurable violation events, and choose budgets \(\varepsilon_i\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^m\varepsilon_i\le\varepsilon\). If \(\mathbb P(V_i(x))\le\varepsilon_i\) for every \(i\), then the first Bonferroni inequality gives
\[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^mV_i(x)\right)\le\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb P(V_i(x))\le\sum_{i=1}^m\varepsilon_i\le\varepsilon.\]
Equivalently, with satisfaction events \(S_i(x)=V_i(x)^c\), one obtains \(\mathbb P(\bigcap_iS_i(x))\ge1-\varepsilon\), without any independence assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocating total risk across individual violations yields a dependence-free sufficient condition for joint reliability through the union bound.

notation.meaning: Risk budget allocated to violation i.

children.title: Fixed Risk Budgets

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Risk Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility condition induced by exogenously specified component risk budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix constants \(\bar\varepsilon_i\in[0,1]\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^m\bar\varepsilon_i\le\varepsilon\), and let \(V_i(x)\) denote measurable violation events. The fixed-budget feasible set is
\[X_{\mathrm{fix}}=\left\{x\in X:\mathbb P(V_i(x))\le\bar\varepsilon_i\ \text{for every }i=1,\ldots,m\right\}.\]
Every \(x\in X_{\mathrm{fix}}\) satisfies \(\mathbb P(\bigcup_iV_i(x))\le\varepsilon\). The budgets are parameters rather than decision variables, so feasibility can be lost even when a different allocation with the same total budget would certify the same decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed component budgets define marginal chance constraints whose feasibility guarantees the joint reliability target through the union bound.

notation.meaning: Exogenously fixed risk budget for component i.

children.title: Uniform Risk Budgets

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Risk Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equal division of the total violation budget among component constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(m\ge1\) measurable violation events \(V_i(x)\) and total budget \(\varepsilon\in[0,1]\), the uniform allocation sets \(\bar\varepsilon_i=\varepsilon/m\) for every \(i\). Hence the uniformly allocated feasible set is
\[X_{\mathrm{unif}}=\left\{x\in X:\mathbb P(V_i(x))\le\frac{\varepsilon}{m}\ \text{for all }i=1,\ldots,m\right\}.\]
Because \(\sum_i\bar\varepsilon_i=\varepsilon\), every \(x\in X_{\mathrm{unif}}\) obeys \(\mathbb P(\bigcup_iV_i(x))\le\varepsilon\). This allocation remains sufficient without symmetry or independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform allocation assigns each of m violations the budget epsilon divided by m, producing a simple dependence-free sufficient condition for joint reliability.

children.title: Budget Feasibility Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Budget Feasibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and nontriviality of bounded individual risk allocations under a total violation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(m\ge 1\), a total budget \(\alpha\ge 0\), and bounds \(0\le \underline\alpha_i\le \overline\alpha_i\), define \[\mathcal B(\alpha)=\left\{a\in\mathbb R^m:\underline\alpha_i\le a_i\le\overline\alpha_i\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,m,\quad \sum_{i=1}^m a_i\le\alpha\right\}.\] Then \(\mathcal B(\alpha)\neq\varnothing\) if and only if \(\sum_{i=1}^m\underline\alpha_i\le\alpha\). If equality holds, its unique member is \(a_i=\underline\alpha_i\) for every \(i\). If the inequality is strict, an allocation distinct from the lower-bound vector exists if and only if \(\overline\alpha_i>\underline\alpha_i\) for at least one \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded risk allocation exists exactly when the mandatory component budgets fit within the total budget. Equality forces the lower-bound allocation, while a distinct allocation additionally requires slack in at least one component upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B(\alpha)\neq\varnothing\iff\sum_{i=1}^m\underline\alpha_i\le\alpha\), and a feasible \(a\neq(\underline\alpha_i)_{i=1}^m\) exists iff \(\sum_i\underline\alpha_i<\alpha\) and \(\overline\alpha_i>\underline\alpha_i\) for some \(i\).

notation.meaning: risk budget allocated to event or constraint i

children.title: Allocation Conservatism

knowledge_statements.title: Allocation Conservatism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservatism introduced by componentwise budgets and the union bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_1(x),\ldots,E_m(x)\) be violation events and let \(\alpha\in[0,1]\). If nonnegative budgets \(a_i\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(E_i(x))\le a_i\) and \(\sum_i a_i\le\alpha\), then \(\mathbb P(\bigcup_iE_i(x))\le\alpha\). Hence the budgeted feasible set is contained in the joint-chance feasible set. The containment can be strict: if \(E_1=\cdots=E_m=E\) with \(\mathbb P(E)=\delta\le\alpha<m\delta\), the joint constraint is feasible although no budgets can dominate all marginal probabilities while summing to at most \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Risk allocation is safe but may reject feasible decisions because it counts overlapping violation events separately.

notation.meaning: violation event for component i at decision x

knowledge_statements.title: Optimized Risk Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk budgets treated as decision variables in a conservative joint-chance formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For violation events \(E_i(x)\) and total tolerance \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), the optimized-budget inner approximation is the projection onto \(x\) of \[\left\{(x,a):a\in\mathbb R_+^m,\ \sum_{i=1}^m a_i\le\alpha,\ \mathbb P(E_i(x))\le a_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,m)\right\}.\] Every projected decision satisfies \(\mathbb P(\bigcup_iE_i(x))\le\alpha\). When each marginal chance constraint is replaced by a budget-dependent safe surrogate \(\phi_i(x,a_i)\le0\), joint optimization over \((x,a)\) selects the allocation rather than fixing it in advance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimized allocation makes component risk budgets variables while retaining a total-budget constraint and union-bound safety.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependence-Blind Conservatism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information lost when a joint violation probability is bounded using only marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(m\ge2\) and \(0<\delta\le1/m\). There exist events with identical marginals \(\mathbb P(E_i)=\delta\) but different union probabilities. If all events coincide, then \(\mathbb P(\bigcup_iE_i)=\delta\); if they are pairwise disjoint, then \(\mathbb P(\bigcup_iE_i)=m\delta\). Thus marginal probabilities alone cannot distinguish these dependence structures, and the dependence-blind bound \(\mathbb P(\bigcup_iE_i)\le\sum_i\mathbb P(E_i)=m\delta\) is sharp over all joint laws but can overestimate the actual union probability by a factor \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal marginals can produce union risks from delta to m delta, so dependence-blind allocation can be sharply conservative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(E_i)=\delta\ \forall i\) does not determine \(\mathbb P(\bigcup_iE_i)\); both \(\delta\) and \(m\delta\) are attainable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coincident-versus-disjoint construction is correct and appropriately records a dependence-blind failure boundary, but no inspectable source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Moment Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cantelli's inequality and its resulting safe scalar chance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be a real random variable with finite mean \(\mu\) and variance \(\sigma^2\). For every \(t>0\), Cantelli's inequality gives \[\mathbb P(Z-\mu\ge t)\le\frac{\sigma^2}{\sigma^2+t^2}.\] Consequently, for \(0<\varepsilon<1\), the deterministic condition \[\mu+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{1-\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}}\le0\] implies \(\mathbb P(Z>0)\le\varepsilon\), and therefore \(\mathbb P(Z\le0)\ge1-\varepsilon\). The implication uses only the first two moments and requires no distributional-form assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cantelli's inequality converts a mean and variance into a safe one-sided chance-constraint approximation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical Cantelli one-sided Chebyshev inequality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Cantelli's inequality and the stated safe implication are correct, including the degenerate zero-variance case, but this theorem requires an authoritative theorem or page locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion–Exclusion Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bonferroni truncations for the probability of a finite union.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For measurable events \(E_1,\ldots,E_m\), let \(S_k=\sum_{1\le i_1<\cdots<i_k\le m}\mathbb P(E_{i_1}\cap\cdots\cap E_{i_k})\). Whenever \(2r\le m\), the Bonferroni inequalities give \[\sum_{k=1}^{2r}(-1)^{k+1}S_k\le\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^mE_i\right)\le\sum_{k=1}^{2r-1}(-1)^{k+1}S_k.\] With all \(m\) terms, inclusion–exclusion is exact: \[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^mE_i\right)=\sum_{k=1}^{m}(-1)^{k+1}S_k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating truncations of inclusion–exclusion provide lower and upper bounds on a finite union probability.

notation.meaning: sum of probabilities of all k-fold event intersections

source_refs.locator: 6.5 Combined Use of Inclusion-Exclusion and Simulation to Estimate the Probability of a Composite Event p. 191

knowledge_statements.title: Dependency-Graph Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A second-moment union bound whose variance terms are localized by an event dependency graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_1,\ldots,E_m\) be measurable events, let \(I_i=\mathbf 1_{E_i}\), and set \(W=\sum_{i=1}^m I_i\). Let \(G=(V,F)\), with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), be a dependency graph for the indicators: whenever two disjoint vertex sets \(A,B\subseteq V\) have no edge between them, the families \((I_i)_{i\in A}\) and \((I_j)_{j\in B}\) are independent. If \(\lambda=\mathbb E[W]>0\), then \[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^mE_i\right)=\mathbb P(W>0)\ge\max\left\{0,1-\frac{\operatorname{Var}(W)}{\lambda^2}\right\},\] where \[\operatorname{Var}(W)=\sum_{i=1}^m\operatorname{Var}(I_i)+2\sum_{\{i,j\}\in F}\operatorname{Cov}(I_i,I_j).\] Thus nonadjacent pairs make no covariance contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For events admitting a dependency graph, nonadjacent indicators have zero covariance, so a second-moment lower bound for the union probability uses only vertex variances and adjacent-pair covariances.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,F)\), with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), is a dependency graph for their indicators.

notation.meaning: dependency graph on the event indices

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Chebyshev zero-count bound plus dependency-graph covariance decomposition

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Information Conservatism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness and distribution-specific conservatism of a two-moment one-sided bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\sigma>0\) and \(t>0\). The two-point random variable \(X\) taking \(t\) with probability \(\sigma^2/(\sigma^2+t^2)\) and \(-\sigma^2/t\) otherwise has mean zero, variance \(\sigma^2\), and \[\mathbb P(X\ge t)=\frac{\sigma^2}{\sigma^2+t^2}.\] Hence Cantelli's bound is sharp over all distributions sharing only those two moments. Any uniformly smaller bound requires additional information, such as support, symmetry, unimodality, or an exponential-moment constraint; for a specified distribution, the moment-only bound may therefore be conservative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cantelli's bound is unimprovable from mean and variance alone, although it may be loose for a known distribution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit extremal distribution attaining Cantelli's inequality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-point construction has the stated mean and variance and attains Cantelli's bound, so it fits the failure-boundary container. An authoritative locator is still required for the sharpness claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Chernoff-Type Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-Markov inner approximation of a scalar chance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x,\xi)\) be measurable, let \(0<\varepsilon<1\), and define \(D_x=\{\theta>0:\mathbb E[e^{\theta g(x,\xi)}]<\infty\}\). For every \(\theta\in D_x\), \[\mathbb P(g(x,\xi)>0)\le\mathbb E[e^{\theta g(x,\xi)}].\] Consequently, if \(D_x\neq\varnothing\), the condition \[\inf_{\theta\in D_x}\mathbb E[e^{\theta g(x,\xi)}]\le\varepsilon\] safely implies \(\mathbb P(g(x,\xi)\le0)\ge1-\varepsilon\). A stronger, directly enforceable sufficient condition is the existence of \(\theta\in D_x\) satisfying \(\log\mathbb E[e^{\theta g(x,\xi)}]\le\log\varepsilon\); equivalence with the infimum condition requires attainment of the infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Chernoff approximation bounds violation probability by the infimum of finite positive exponential moments. Enforcing the bound at one positive parameter is sufficient, and is equivalent to the infimum condition only when a minimizer exists.

notation.meaning: domain of finite positive exponential moments at decision x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exponential Markov inequality and Chernoff optimization

knowledge_statements.title: Bernstein Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bernstein safe approximation for a sum of independent bounded perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) be independent random variables satisfying \(\mathbb E[X_i]=0\), \(X_i\le b\) almost surely for a common \(b>0\), and \(v=\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E[X_i^2]\). For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), set \(L=\log(1/\varepsilon)\). The deterministic condition \[a+\sqrt{2vL}+\frac{bL}{3}\le0\] implies \(\mathbb P(a+\sum_{i=1}^mX_i>0)\le\varepsilon\), and hence safely implies \(\mathbb P(a+\sum_{i=1}^mX_i\le0)\ge1-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bernstein's inequality gives a safe constraint using the mean offset, aggregate variance, boundedness, and target risk.

notation.meaning: deterministic offset in the scalar random constraint

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard inverted Bernstein concentration inequality

knowledge_statements.title: Exponential-Moment Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cumulant-generating-function interface for constructing Chernoff-safe constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a measurable scalar random constraint \(g(x,\xi)\), define \(D_x=\{\theta>0:\mathbb E[e^{\theta g(x,\xi)}]<\infty\}\) and \(K_x(\theta)=\log\mathbb E[e^{\theta g(x,\xi)}]\) for \(\theta\in D_x\). If \(0<\varepsilon<1\) and \(D_x\neq\varnothing\), then \[\inf_{\theta\in D_x}\{K_x(\theta)-\log\varepsilon\}\le0\] is a Chernoff-safe condition for \(\mathbb P(g(x,\xi)\le0)\ge1-\varepsilon\). Existence of \(\theta\in D_x\) with \(K_x(\theta)\le\log\varepsilon\) is a stronger sufficient interface and is equivalent to the infimum condition when the infimum is attained. If \(\widehat K_x(\theta)\ge K_x(\theta)\), imposing \(\widehat K_x(\theta)\le\log\varepsilon\) for some \(\theta\in D_x\) is also safe.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cumulant-generating function supports an infimum-based Chernoff condition, while a formula, upper bound, or oracle can enforce the bound at a particular positive parameter. These interfaces are equivalent only when the infimum is attained.

knowledge_statements.title: Average Value-at-Risk Inner Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper-tail AVaR surrogate for a scalar chance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z=g(x,\xi)\) be integrable and let \(0<\varepsilon<1\) denote the allowed upper-tail probability. Define upper-tail average value-at-risk by \[\operatorname{AVaR}_{\varepsilon}(Z)=\inf_{t\in\mathbb R}\left\{t+\frac1\varepsilon\mathbb E[(Z-t)_+]\right\}.\] Since the upper \((1-\varepsilon)\)-quantile does not exceed \(\operatorname{AVaR}_{\varepsilon}(Z)\), the condition \(\operatorname{AVaR}_{\varepsilon}(g(x,\xi))\le0\) implies \(\mathbb P(g(x,\xi)\le0)\ge1-\varepsilon\). Equivalently, the inner approximation introduces \(t\) and requires \(t+\varepsilon^{-1}\mathbb E[(g(x,\xi)-t)_+]\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requiring upper-tail AVaR to be nonpositive safely enforces the corresponding scalar chance constraint.

positive part max of u and zero

knowledge_statements.title: Optimized Certainty-Equivalent Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective risk surrogate for a scalar chance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z_x=g(x,\xi)\) and require \(\mathbb P(Z_x>0)\leq\varepsilon\). For a nondecreasing convex function \(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\) satisfying \(\phi(0)=1\) and \(\phi(s)\geq1\) for \(s>0\), define
\[
B_\phi(x)=\inf_{t>0}\mathbb E\!\left[\phi\!\left(\frac{Z_x}{t}\right)\right].
\]
Then \(\mathbb P(Z_x>0)\leq B_\phi(x)\). Consequently, \(B_\phi(x)\leq\varepsilon\) is sufficient for the chance constraint. The existence of \(t>0\) satisfying
\[
t\mathbb E[\phi(Z_x/t)]-t\varepsilon\leq0
\]
also implies \(B_\phi(x)\leq\varepsilon\). Conversely, such a scale exists whenever \(B_\phi(x)<\varepsilon\), or when \(B_\phi(x)=\varepsilon\) and the infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing the positive scale gives an upper bound on violation probability. A feasible scale certifies the chance constraint, while equivalence at the boundary additionally requires attainment of the infimum.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_x=g(x,\xi)\) is measurable and the displayed expectations are finite.
\(\phi\) is nondecreasing, convex, nonnegative, \(\phi(0)=1\), and \(\phi(s)\geq1\) for \(s>0\).

children.title: Risk-Surrogate Tightness
children.top_down_role: Gap between a risk-based inner approximation and the underlying chance constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Surrogate Tightness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive tightness of a safe generating-function surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Z=g(x,\xi)\), define \(p(x)=\mathbb P(Z>0)\) and \(B_\phi(x)=\inf_{t>0}\mathbb E[\phi(Z/t)]\), where \(\phi(s)\geq\mathbf 1_{(0,\infty)}(s)\). The additive tightness gap is
\[
\Delta_\phi(x)=B_\phi(x)-p(x)\geq0.
\]
If the infimum is attained at \(t_x>0\), then
\[
\Delta_\phi(x)=\mathbb E\!\left[\phi(Z/t_x)-\mathbf 1_{(0,\infty)}(Z)\right].
\]
Thus smaller nonnegative excess majorization on the distribution of \(Z/t_x\) means a tighter safe approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Surrogate tightness is the nonnegative gap between the optimized probability upper bound and the true violation probability.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is measurable and the surrogate expectations are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_\phi(x)\geq0\), with the displayed expectation formula when an optimizer \(t_x\) exists.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the gap identity follows directly from the surrogate definition and indicator majorization

children.title: Risk-Surrogate Scaling
children.top_down_role: Dependence of surrogate behavior on dimension, confidence level, and normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Surrogate Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive scale optimization within a perspective probability surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(x\), let
\[
H_x(t)=\mathbb E\!\left[\phi\!\left(\frac{g(x,\xi)}{t}\right)\right],\qquad t>0.
\]
A risk-surrogate scale is any \(t_x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{t>0}H_x(t)\). If the minimum is not attained, then for each \(\eta>0\), an \(\eta\)-optimal scale is any \(t_{x,\eta}>0\) satisfying
\[
H_x(t_{x,\eta})\leq\inf_{t>0}H_x(t)+\eta.
\]
For a selected scale \(t>0\), the perspective constraint is \(tH_x(t)-t\varepsilon\leq0\), equivalently \(H_x(t)\leq\varepsilon\). Optimizing the scale can improve surrogate tightness without changing the safety implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact minimizing scale is used when it exists; otherwise any positive-tolerance approximate minimizer may be used. Scale optimization can reduce conservatism without invalidating safety.
assumptions_latex: \(t>0\), and all displayed expectations are finite.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: approximate minimizers exist for every positive tolerance when the infimum is finite
authoritative source required for the perspective scaling convention

children.title: Exactness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structured settings where a risk surrogate matches the target chance constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness criterion for an optimized indicator-majorizing surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p(x)=\mathbb P(Z>0)\) and \(B_\phi(x)=\inf_{t>0}\mathbb E[\phi(Z/t)]\). The surrogate is exact at \(x\) precisely when
\[
\inf_{t>0}\mathbb E\!\left[\phi(Z/t)-\mathbf 1_{(0,\infty)}(Z)\right]=0.
\]
If a minimizing scale \(t_x>0\) exists, exactness is equivalent to
\[
\phi(Z/t_x)=\mathbf 1_{(0,\infty)}(Z)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Consequently, exactness can occur when the scaled support of \(Z\) lies entirely in the contact set where \(\phi\) equals the violation indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The safe surrogate is exact exactly when its expected excess over the violation indicator can be driven to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is measurable and the relevant expectations are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_\phi(x)=p(x)\) exactly under the displayed zero-excess condition.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a nonnegative random variable has zero expectation exactly when it vanishes almost surely

children.title: High-Confidence Conservatism

knowledge_statements.title: High-Confidence Conservatism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservatism of safe surrogates at small violation tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_\varepsilon=\{x:B_\phi(x)\leq\varepsilon\}\) and \(C_\varepsilon=\{x:p(x)\leq\varepsilon\}\), where \(p(x)=\mathbb P(g(x,\xi)>0)\) and \(B_\phi(x)\geq p(x)\). Then
\[
F_\varepsilon\subseteq C_\varepsilon.
\]
Writing \(\Delta_\phi(x)=B_\phi(x)-p(x)\), surrogate feasibility is equivalent to \(p(x)+\Delta_\phi(x)\leq\varepsilon\). Hence at high confidence, where \(\varepsilon\) is small, even a modest positive gap can exclude chance-feasible decisions; exactness requires the gap to vanish at the relevant decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Safe surrogate feasibility remains sufficient at high confidence, but a positive approximation gap consumes the small violation budget and may be strongly conservative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_\varepsilon\subseteq C_\varepsilon\), and the surrogate consumes \(\Delta_\phi(x)\) of the violation budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Multivariate Probability Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral representation used by joint chance-constraint probability oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi\in\mathbb R^d\) have density \(f\), and let \(A(x)=\{z\in\mathbb R^d:g_j(x,z)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). The joint satisfaction probability is
\[
p(x)=\mathbb P(\xi\in A(x))=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\mathbf 1_{A(x)}(z)f(z)\,dz=\int_{A(x)}f(z)\,dz.
\]
For a rectangular event \(A(x)=\prod_{i=1}^d[a_i(x),b_i(x)]\), this becomes a multivariate rectangular probability integral, which a numerical probability oracle approximates to a prescribed absolute or relative tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint chance probability is a multivariate density integral over the decision-dependent satisfaction region.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a probability density on \(\mathbb R^d\).

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo Probability Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic low-discrepancy evaluation after transformation to a unit cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a measurable transformation \(T:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb R^d\) with \(T(U)\) distributed as \(\xi\) for \(U\sim\mathrm{Unif}([0,1]^d)\), choose low-discrepancy points \(u_1,\ldots,u_N\) and compute
\[
\widehat p_N(x)=\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N\mathbf 1_{A(x)}(T(u_n)).
\]
Return \(\widehat p_N(x)\) when a prescribed sample budget or discrepancy criterion is met. If \(h_x(u)=\mathbf 1_{A(x)}(T(u))\) has bounded Hardy--Krause variation, then
\[
|\widehat p_N(x)-p(x)|\leq V_{\mathrm{HK}}(h_x)D_N^*.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transform low-discrepancy cube points to the uncertainty distribution and average the event indicator; bounded variation gives a discrepancy error bound.
assumptions_latex: The stated bound requires finite Hardy--Krause variation of \(h_x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat p_N(x)\) estimates \(p(x)\), with error at most \(V_{\mathrm{HK}}(h_x)D_N^*\) under bounded variation.

knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Sampling Probability Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Likelihood-ratio Monte Carlo evaluation of rare satisfaction or violation probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p=\mathbb P_f(\xi\in A)=\int_A f(z)\,dz\), and choose a proposal density \(q\) satisfying \(q(z)>0\) wherever \(f(z)\mathbf 1_A(z)>0\). Draw independent samples \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\sim q\) and compute
\[
\widehat p_N=\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N\mathbf 1_A(Z_n)\frac{f(Z_n)}{q(Z_n)}.
\]
Return \(\widehat p_N\) as the importance-sampling probability estimate. Then \(\mathbb E_q[\widehat p_N]=p\), and
\[
\operatorname{Var}_q(\widehat p_N)=\frac1N\left(\int_A\frac{f(z)^2}{q(z)}\,dz-p^2\right),
\]
provided the second moment is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Draw samples from a proposal emphasizing the event, weight each event occurrence by the likelihood ratio, and average the weights to obtain an unbiased probability estimate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E_q[\widehat p_N]=p\), with the displayed variance.

knowledge_statements.title: Analytic Probability Gradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Score-function differentiation for a parameterized probability density.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
p(x)=\int_A f(z;x)\,dz,
\]
where the measurable event \(A\) is independent of \(x\). If differentiation may be interchanged with integration and \(f(z;x)>0\) on its support, then
\[
\nabla p(x)=\int_A\nabla_x f(z;x)\,dz
=\mathbb E_x\!\left[\mathbf 1_A(\xi)\nabla_x\log f(\xi;x)\right].
\]
This score representation is an analytic probability gradient. If the event boundary also depends on \(x\), an additional boundary-transport term is generally required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed event and differentiable parameterized density, the probability gradient is the expected event indicator times the density score.
assumptions_latex: \(f(\cdot;x)\) is differentiable in \(x\), with an integrable local dominating function.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: differentiation under the integral sign and the identity \(\nabla f=f\nabla\log f\) give the representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-event score representation is mathematically correct under the interchange and support assumptions, but a specific probability-sensitivity source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Simulation-Based Probability Gradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monte Carlo score estimator for a probability gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(p(x)=\mathbb P_x(\xi\in A)\), draw independent \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\sim f(\cdot;x)\) and compute
\[
\widehat{\nabla p}_N(x)=\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N\mathbf 1_A(\xi_n)\nabla_x\log f(\xi_n;x).
\]
Return the estimate when the sample budget is exhausted or a confidence-based standard-error criterion is met. Under the score-representation hypotheses, the estimator is unbiased; if its summand has finite second moment, its covariance equals the summand covariance divided by \(N\), and it converges almost surely to \(\nabla p(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average event-weighted density scores from simulation to obtain an unbiased, consistent probability-gradient estimate.
assumptions_latex: The analytic score representation for \(\nabla p(x)\) is valid.
The score-weighted indicator has finite second moment.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Probability Subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke generalized gradients for locally Lipschitz probability maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz, and let \(D_p\) be the set where \(p\) is differentiable. Its Clarke probability subdifferential at \(x\) is
\[
\partial_Cp(x)=\operatorname{conv}\left\{\lim_{k\to\infty}\nabla p(x_k):x_k\to x,\ x_k\in D_p\right\},
\]
where limits are taken over convergent gradient sequences. Every \(v\in\partial_Cp(x)\) satisfies
\[
p^\circ(x;d)\geq v^{\mathsf T}d\quad\text{for all }d\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
with \(p^\circ\) the Clarke directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a nonsmooth probability map, generalized gradients are convex combinations of limiting nearby gradients and support every Clarke directional derivative.
assumptions_latex: The ambient decision space is finite-dimensional.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke Generalized Gradient of a Smoothed Probability Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity and generalized-gradient formula for a kernel-smoothed nonseparable probability function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that the density \(k\) is nonnegative, bounded, and continuous. For every \(z\in\mathbb R^s\), let each \(g_i(\cdot,z)\) be concave, and suppose that for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(\delta>0\), and \(i=1,\ldots,m\), the local subgradients satisfy \[\sup\{\|s\|:s\in\partial g_i(y,z),\ \|y-x\|\leq\delta\}\leq l_\delta(x,z),\] where \(l_\delta(x,\cdot)\) is integrable. Then \(G_\varepsilon\) is Lipschitz continuous and Clarke-regular, and \[{\partial}^{\circ}G_\varepsilon(x)=\frac1\varepsilon\int_{\mathbb R^s}k\!\left(\frac{g_M(x,z)-c}{\varepsilon}\right)\operatorname{conv}\{\partial g_i(x,z):i\in I(x,z)\}\,dP_Z.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative bounded continuous smoothing density, concavity of the component functions, and an integrable uniform local bound on their subgradients make the smoothed probability function Lipschitz and Clarke-regular; its Clarke generalized gradient is the probability integral of the convex hull of active component subgradients, weighted by the smoothing kernel.

l_\delta(x,\cdot)\text{ is integrable for every }x\in\mathcal X\text{ and }\delta>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_\varepsilon\text{ is Lipschitz and Clarke-regular, and }{\partial}^{\circ}G_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^{-1}\int k\!\left(\frac{g_M(x,z)-c}{\varepsilon}\right)\operatorname{conv}\{\partial g_i(x,z):i\in I(x,z)\}\,dP_Z

children.title: Probability Barrier Methods
children.top_down_role: Interior formulations that discourage approach to chance-constraint boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Probability Barrier Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior method for a differentiable chance-probability constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min_{x\in X}f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad p(x)\geq1-\varepsilon,
\]
choose a strictly feasible \(x_0\) and parameters \(\mu_0>0\), \(\theta\in(0,1)\). At outer iteration \(k\), approximately minimize
\[
F_{\mu_k}(x)=f(x)-\mu_k\log\bigl(p(x)-1+\varepsilon\bigr)
\]
over \(X\cap\{x:p(x)>1-\varepsilon\}\), using \(\nabla F_{\mu_k}(x)=\nabla f(x)-\mu_k\nabla p(x)/(p(x)-1+\varepsilon)\). Set \(\mu_{k+1}=\theta\mu_k\), preserve strict feasibility by line search, and stop when optimization residuals and \(\mu_k\) meet their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a logarithmic barrier to the positive probability margin, solve decreasing-barrier subproblems, and keep all iterates strictly chance-feasible.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(p\) are continuously differentiable on the strict interior.
A strictly feasible initial point exists.
Each barrier subproblem is solved to a tolerance tending to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm generates strictly feasible iterates while \(\mu_k\downarrow0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Probability Penalty Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exterior penalty formulation for a single scalar chance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) be nondecreasing, satisfy \(\psi(0)=0\), and satisfy \(\psi(t)>0\) for every \(t>0\). Select \(0<\rho_0<\rho_1<\cdots\). At iteration \(k\), approximately minimize
\[P_{\rho_k}(x)=f(x)+\rho_k\,\psi\bigl([p(x)-\alpha]_+\bigr)\quad\text{over }x\in X,\]
using the preceding iterate as the initial point, and obtain \(x_k\) satisfying the prescribed optimization residual tolerance. Stop and return \(x_k\) when both \(p(x_k)\leq\alpha+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\) and the optimization residual tolerance hold; otherwise increase the penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize objectives that penalize excess violation probability with successively larger weights, and return an iterate only when both chance feasibility and the prescribed optimization-residual test hold.
assumptions_latex: The permitted violation probability is \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned iterate satisfies \(p(x_k)\leq\alpha+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\) and the prescribed optimization residual tolerance for the current penalized problem.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz near \(x^*\in F\), and the stated local error bound holds there. Then, for every \(\rho>L\kappa\), \(x^*\) is a local minimizer of
\[P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho[p(x)-\alpha]_+\quad\text{over }x\in X.\]
Conversely, any local minimizer \(\bar x\) of \(P_\rho\) lying in the error-bound neighborhood and satisfying \(p(\bar x)\leq\alpha\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(F\). Thus sufficiently large finite penalty parameters recover local constrained minima without taking \(\rho\) to infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local error bound makes the linear probability penalty exact: every penalty weight above the objective-Lipschitz and error-bound threshold preserves the constrained local minimizer.

children.title: Barrier-Parameter Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Conditioning and boundary-resolution effects associated with barrier parameter choices.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(p\) are twice continuously differentiable near a strictly feasible point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The barrier curvature contains terms of orders \(\mu/s(x)\) and \(\mu/s(x)^2\), so conditioning can deteriorate as the slack vanishes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning of the logarithmic barrier for a smooth scalar probability constraint.

source_refs.locator: 1.4.8 Penalty and barrier function methods p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the logarithmic probability barrier
\[B_\mu(x)=f(x)-\mu\log s(x),\qquad s(x)=\alpha-p(x),\]
the derivatives are
\[
abla B_\mu(x)=
abla f(x)+ rac{\mu}{s(x)}
abla p(x)\]
and
\[
abla^2B_\mu(x)=
abla^2f(x)+ rac{\mu}{s(x)}
abla^2p(x)+ rac{\mu}{s(x)^2}
abla p(x)
abla p(x)^{\mathsf T}.\]
Hence approaching the boundary with \(s(x)\downarrow0\) amplifies gradient and curvature contributions unless \(\mu\) is reduced compatibly. In particular, the rank-one term can create a large Hessian eigenvalue proportional to \(\mu\lVert
abla p(x)Vert^2/s(x)^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a log barrier, derivatives scale inversely with probability slack; near the chance boundary, curvature can grow quadratically in inverse slack and impair numerical conditioning.
knowledge_statements.title: Barrier-Parameter Conditioning

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(C_0\supseteq C\). At iteration \(k\), compute
\[x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C_k}f(x).\]
If the chance-feasibility oracle certifies \(x_k\in C\), return \(x_k\). Otherwise obtain \((a_k,b_k)\) satisfying \(a_k^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_k\) for every \(x\in C\) but \(a_k^{\mathsf T}x_k>b_k\), and set
\[C_{k+1}=C_k\cap\{x:a_k^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_k\}.\]
Stop instead when the relaxation bound and incumbent value differ by at most the prescribed tolerance. Validity of every supporting halfspace preserves \(C\subseteq C_k\) throughout.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve successive outer relaxations of the convex chance-feasible set, separating each infeasible trial point by a valid supporting hyperplane until feasibility or a bound tolerance is reached.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a feasible \(x_k\), construct convex models \(\widehat f_k\) and \(\widehat h_k\) satisfying \(\widehat h_k(x_k)=h(x_k)\), first-order agreement at \(x_k\), and \(h(x)\leq\widehat h_k(x)\) on the trust region. Compute
\[d_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d}\{\widehat f_k(x_k+d):x_k+d\in X,\ \widehat h_k(x_k+d)\leq0,\ \lVert d\rVert\leq\Delta_k\}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_0\in X\), \(\lambda_0\geq0\), and positive step sizes \(\tau_k,\sigma_k\). A projected primal-dual probability iteration is
\[x_{k+1}=\Pi_X\bigl(x_k-\tau_k[\nabla f(x_k)+\lambda_k\nabla p(x_k)]\bigr),\]
\[\lambda_{k+1}=\bigl[\lambda_k+\sigma_k(p(x_{k+1})-\alpha)\bigr]_+.\]
An alternative exact primal step minimizes \(L(\cdot,\lambda_k)\) over \(X\). Stop when primal feasibility, projected primal stationarity, and complementarity residual \(\lambda_k[p(x_k)-\alpha]\) are all within specified tolerances; return \((x_k,\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate a primal step that prices probability violation with a nonnegative multiplier and a projected dual step that raises the price when the chance constraint is violated.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Probability Methods

source_witnesses.locator: 1.7.4 A Dual Decomposition Method p. 75

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projected gradient primal-dual iteration is not the same method as the cited dual-decomposition section, and no direct source supports its chance-constraint specialization. The complementarity stopping residual should also be specified as a nonnegative norm or absolute residual rather than the signed product alone.

children.title: Branching Strategies
children.top_down_role: Branching choices tailored to discrete chance-constrained formulations.

assumptions_latex: The current branch-and-bound node has a mixed-integer relaxation with integer index set \(I\).
A relaxation solution \(\bar x\) is available, together with probability-violation information.
Every child disjunction preserves all integer-feasible solutions of the parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Branching partitions the parent node into valid children while prioritizing variables or disjunctions expected to improve chance-feasibility bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic branch-and-cut branching with probability-aware scoring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each fractional integer variable \(j\in I\), form two child relaxations by adding
\[x_j\leq\lfloor\bar x_j\rfloor\qquad\text{or}\qquad x_j\geq\lceil\bar x_j\rceil.\]
Estimate each child's bound improvement and probability-feasibility improvement, and assign a score \(S_j\) from these estimates, such as a weighted combination or the product of the two child improvements. Branch on an index maximizing \(S_j\). More general chance-structure disjunctions may replace variable branching only when their union contains every integer-feasible parent solution. Fathom a child when its relaxation is infeasible or its bound cannot improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition a node with valid integer disjunctions, ranking candidates by predicted objective-bound and chance-feasibility improvement, then discard children that are infeasible or dominated by the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching Strategies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Variable branching itself is standard, but the proposed probability-aware score and chance-structure disjunctions are formulation dependent and have no cited evidence. A source must define or validate the scoring rule and its applicability to chance-constrained branch-and-cut.

children.title: Cut Generation
children.top_down_role: Families of valid cuts used to strengthen chance-constrained formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(R\) is a relaxation containing every feasible mixed-integer chance-constrained point.
A separation routine identifies a valid inequality violated by a relaxation solution \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding the separating inequality removes \(\bar x\) without excluding any feasible point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract validity contract for chance-constraint cuts in branch-and-cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Solve the current relaxation \(R\) and obtain \(\bar x\). If a chance-feasibility or combinatorial separation oracle returns \((a,b)\) such that
\[a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\quad\text{for every feasible mixed-integer chance-constrained }x,\qquad a^{\mathsf T}\bar x>b,\]
replace \(R\) by \(R\cap\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\}\) and reoptimize. Repeat until no cut exceeding the separation tolerance is found. Globally valid cuts may be retained throughout the search; locally valid cuts remain attached only to the node subtree where their validity assumptions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate a relaxation point with an inequality valid for every feasible chance-constrained integer point, add the cut, and reoptimize until no significant violation remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Generation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract validity contract is correct but does not identify an actual chance-constraint cut family or separation construction. No evidence is supplied for this nontrivial algorithmic leaf.

children.title: Node Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxation structures used within the search tree.

assumptions_latex: The original formulation contains integer variables and a chance-feasibility condition.
At a search node, branching decisions impose additional bounds or disjunction sides.
Selected integrality or chance constraints may be relaxed without excluding feasible descendants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node relaxation gives a valid objective bound for every feasible solution in that node's subtree.

notation.meaning: Feasible set represented by the search node.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer-relaxation bound used at a branch-and-cut node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_N\) be the feasible set of a minimization problem restricted by the decisions defining node \(N\). Construct a tractable set \(R_N\) by relaxing integrality, replacing the chance constraint by a valid outer approximation, and retaining all node restrictions, so that \(F_N\subseteq R_N\). Then
\[L_N=\inf_{x\in R_N}f(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x).\]
Consequently, if \(R_N=\varnothing\), the node is infeasible; and if \(L_N\) is no better than the incumbent objective within tolerance, the entire node may be fathomed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node relaxation contains all feasible descendants, so its optimum is a valid minimization lower bound; infeasible or incumbent-dominated nodes can be discarded.
knowledge_statements.title: Node Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound property follows from the displayed set containment and fits the node-relaxation leaf, but the record supplies neither a source nor a standard-field rationale, and it leaves the chance-constraint outer approximation unspecified.

children.title: Incumbent Feasibility Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation mechanisms for detecting probabilistic infeasibility in candidate solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(\hat x\) is an integer-feasible incumbent candidate.
A probability oracle evaluates or validly bounds \(p(\hat x)=\mathbb{P}(g(\hat x,\xi)>0)\).
A separator can produce a valid cut whenever violation is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent is accepted only after certified chance feasibility; otherwise a valid cut excludes it or its violating pattern.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-based certification and separation of integer incumbent candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\hat x\), compute bounds \(\underline p(\hat x)\leq p(\hat x)\leq\overline p(\hat x)\) valid at the required certification level. If \(\overline p(\hat x)\leq\alpha\), certify chance feasibility and admit \(\hat x\) as an incumbent. If \(\underline p(\hat x)>\alpha\), generate an inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) valid for all chance-feasible integer points and violated by \(\hat x\), add it to the search relaxation, and reject \(\hat x\). If neither test holds, refine probability evaluation rather than declaring feasibility or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept an integer incumbent only when a valid upper bound certifies its violation probability; reject and separate it when a valid lower bound proves violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Feasibility Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three-way logic using valid lower and upper probability bounds is sensible, but the required certification level and probability oracle are undefined, and existence of a valid separating cut is assumed without a formulation or source. The certificate cannot be validated as stated.

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty has finite scenarios \(s=1,\ldots,S\) with probabilities \(q_s>0\).
Scenario constraints are \(g_s(x)\leq0\), and binary variables \(z_s\) may mark ignored scenarios.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixing or dualizing the shared variables separates the scenario constraints into independent blocks coupled only by nonanticipativity and the violation budget.

notation.meaning: Indicator that scenario s may violate its constraint.
Permitted total probability of ignored scenarios.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support decomposition using scenario indicators and a probability budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With valid constants \(M_s\), the finite-support chance constraint has the mixed-integer representation
\[g_s(x)\leq M_sz_s\quad(s=1,\ldots,S),\qquad \sum_{s=1}^S q_sz_s\leq\alpha,\qquad z_s\in\{0,1\}.\]
Introducing scenario copies \(x_sesponsible\) is unnecessary; instead, introduce \(x_s=x\) for each scenario. Conditional on the common decision or after dualizing the equalities \(x_s=x\), each block \(g_s(x_s)\leq M_sz_s\) is scenario-separable. The master problem enforces nonanticipativity and the single weighted violation budget, while scenario subproblems provide feasibility information or cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite uncertainty, scenario indicators and a weighted violation budget represent the chance constraint; scenario copies then separate once their common-decision equalities are fixed or dualized.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-scenario indicator representation and decomposition require a direct source and explicit conditions making each M_s valid. The statement also contains the undefined unsafe command \responsible and a contradictory sentence about whether scenario copies are introduced. These defects require correction after the mathematical formulation is sourced.

assumptions_latex: The base mixing set is \(M=\{(y,z):y+h_iz_i\geq h_i,\ i=1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mixing inequalities strengthen the linear relaxation by coupling the continuous recourse or safety variable with ordered scenario indicators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical single-row mixing-set relaxation underlying scenario-based chance formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constraints defining \(M\) are equivalently \(y\geq h_i(1-z_i)\) for all \(i\). Their continuous relaxation permits weak fractional combinations because each scenario row is enforced separately. A mixing-set relaxation augments that relaxation with valid inequalities derived from the ordered thresholds \(h_1\leq\cdots\leq h_n\), coupling several components of \(z\) with \(y\). For any selected index sequence, the inequality coefficients must be chosen so that every binary point of \(M\) satisfies the inequality; the strengthened relaxation is the intersection of the base relaxation with the generated mixing inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordered scenario thresholds create a canonical mixing set. Valid mixing inequalities couple its continuous safety variable with multiple binary scenario indicators and tighten the separate-row linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixing-Set Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The canonical mixing-set setup is plausible, but the record gives no actual mixing inequality, coefficient formula, theorem, or citation. A direct authoritative source is necessary to determine the exact strengthened relaxation represented by this leaf.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semicontinuity and Consistency of Empirical Violation Probabilities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity, almost-sure epigraphical convergence, and compact-uniform convergence of the empirical violation-probability functions from the chance-constraint setup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $p$ and $\widehat p_N$ be the true and empirical violation-probability functions from the chance-constraint setup. If $C(x,\xi)$ is Carathéodory, then $p$ and $\widehat p_N$ are lower semicontinuous. If the sample is iid, then $\widehat p_N\xrightarrow{e}p$ almost surely. If additionally $\Pr\{C(x,\xi)=0\}=0$ for every $x\in X$, then $p$ is continuous on $X$ and $\widehat p_N\to p$ almost surely uniformly on every compact subset of $X$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The true and empirical violation-probability functions are lower semicontinuous for a Carathéodory constraint function. IID sampling yields almost-sure epigraphical convergence. If every decision has zero probability of lying exactly on the constraint boundary, the true probability is continuous and convergence is almost surely uniform on compact subsets.
assumptions_latex: \text{The sample is iid for the epigraphical-convergence claim}
\Pr\{C(x,\xi)=0\}=0\quad\forall x\in X\text{ for continuity and compact-uniform convergence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p,\widehat p_N\text{ are lower semicontinuous};\quad \widehat p_N\xrightarrow{e}p\text{ a.s.};\quad p\in C(X)\text{ and }\widehat p_N\to p\text{ a.s. uniformly on compact subsets of }X\text{ under the boundary condition}
